bull_bear.body:
- Heritage and trust: more than 150 years in the global jute industry, tracing back to 1872 when Fort Gloster Jute Manufacturing Company Limited set up the Gloster Mills
- Stable promoter backing — the Company has grown significantly since coming under The Bangur Group's leadership in 1954
- Integrated manufacturing platform at scale (four integrated units, >175 acres, >4,500 workforce, ~60,000 MT annual capability) enabling operational efficiency, quality consistency and scalability
- Modern imported machinery at the Gloster Nuvo unit enabling a range of value-added products including fine yarns
- Sustainability positioning — jute as a renewable, biodegradable, environmentally friendly natural fibre addressing growing global demand for sustainable alternatives
- Emerging consumer brand extension through PATSAN, connecting the manufacturing heritage to end-user retail markets
- Diversified customer reach across domestic and international markets
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Availability and price of quality raw jute — Flagged by management as a key concern. The raw jute market witnessed an unprecedented surge in prices during the year, caused by unremunerative prices, adverse weather and lower sowing areas, with prices increasing nearly three-fold on lower crop and reduced carry-over stocks; the steep rise in input costs exerted significant pressure on the jute industry. Even in the ensuing season, prices are expected to remain at elevated levels compared to previous years.
- Dilution of the compulsory Jute Packing Order (JPMA) — Compulsory packing norms for food grains and sugar stand at 100% and 20% of production respectively, and the notification is valid only up to 30th June 2026. Any dilution of the compulsory Jute Packing Order can adversely affect the market for jute products — a structural demand-base risk since Government demand is a core end market.
- Export competitiveness and lower export incentives — Management flags that lower incentives on exports impact competitive pricing in export markets. Exports saw further de-growth during the year largely due to the unprecedented increase in prices of finished goods, apart from the effect of wars affecting all export markets.
- Competition from Bangladesh and trade-route restrictions — Management flags the banning of import of specific jute products from Bangladesh via all land routes as a risk/concern, and separately notes export markets already lost to Bangladesh that it hopes to win back only if prices correct.
- Climate change and energy management — BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: jute manufacturing is inherently energy intensive across fibre processing, spinning, weaving and finishing, while jute cultivation is largely rain-fed and highly sensitive to climate variability — erratic monsoons, flooding and rising temperatures can adversely affect raw jute availability, fibre quality and procurement timelines. Regulatory and market expectations to decarbonise add transition risk.
- Emission management — BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: operations generate emissions from boilers, generators and fibre handling including particulate matter and combustion-related emissions. Inadequate control may cause regulatory non-compliance, penalties, operational disruption and reputational damage, heightened by customer focus on environmentally responsible sourcing.
- Water and effluent management — BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: water is a critical input in batching, softening and washing. Inefficient use or improper discharge of untreated effluent with high organic load may cause regulatory non-compliance, environmental degradation and community concerns, especially in water-stressed areas.
- Biodiversity impact of industrial operations — BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: land use change, emissions, wastewater discharge and waste disposal can directly or indirectly impact local biodiversity, while jute cultivation itself depends on healthy agro-ecosystems, making biodiversity conservation material to long-term resource security.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Gloster Limited manufactures jute goods and allied products and is managed organizationally as a single business. Its integrated operations at Bauria, Howrah, West Bengal span four business units over more than 175 acres, supported by a workforce of more than 4,500 persons, and serve customers in India and outside India across industrial packaging, government procurement and, increasingly, consumer lifestyle markets. Building on this manufacturing base, the Company has embarked on a retail journey through PATSAN, its dedicated consumer brand for sustainable jute lifestyle and home products.

- Heritage and trust: more than 150 years in the global jute industry, tracing back to 1872 when Fort Gloster Jute Manufacturing Company Limited set up the Gloster Mills
- Stable promoter backing — the Company has grown significantly since coming under The Bangur Group's leadership in 1954
- Integrated manufacturing platform at scale (four integrated units, >175 acres, >4,500 workforce, ~60,000 MT annual capability) enabling operational efficiency, quality consistency and scalability
- Modern imported machinery at the Gloster Nuvo unit enabling a range of value-added products including fine yarns
- Sustainability positioning — jute as a renewable, biodegradable, environmentally friendly natural fibre addressing growing global demand for sustainable alternatives
- Emerging consumer brand extension through PATSAN, connecting the manufacturing heritage to end-user retail markets
- Diversified customer reach across domestic and international markets
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Improve operational efficiency, enhance productivity and optimise costs while increasing the share of value-added products
- Expand presence in both domestic and international markets, including new markets, with a diversified and value-added jute product portfolio
- Build a retail/consumer business through PATSAN, the dedicated retail brand, to move beyond traditional industrial and institutional markets
- Strengthen PATSAN further through digital innovation, product expansion and customer-centric initiatives, with www.patsan.in as the brand discovery and product showcase platform
- Protect and build brand IP — the PATSAN logo secured trademark registration under Class 24 covering textiles and textile substitutes, household linen, sleeping bags and fabrics for household use
- Drive growth through innovation: modern technology, advanced manufacturing, automated infrastructure and continuous R&D to develop next-generation jute products for packaging, lifestyle, industrial and consumer markets (Jute-Viscose Yarn, Jute Jumbo Bags, polished jute yarns, banana fibre-based fabrics, Ju-Co-Vis textiles)
- Use brand outreach and market development — collaborations with NJB, JCI and NIFT (including a fashion show in Patna with NIFT) and participation in international trade fairs such as Ambiente and Heimtextil, Frankfurt
- Embed sustainability across design, responsible manufacturing, quality assurance and conscious packaging — demand-forecast-led production to minimise overproduction and waste, and packaging that minimises plastic and encourages recyclability
- The Company's stated governance philosophy is to enhance the long-term economic value of the company and deliver sustainable return to its stakeholders, with the Board involved in all important decisions including policy matters, strategic business plans, new avenues of investment and expansion, and major accounting provisions and write-offs. Distribution to shareholders follows an annual Board-recommended final dividend on equity shares, placed before members as ordinary business at the Annual General Meeting; the Board recommended a final dividend for the financial year 2025-26. Remuneration policy is explicitly pay-for-performance and aligned with the business strategy, risk tolerance and long-term interests of the Company, with executive pay affordable on a sustainable basis. Statutory auditors M/s Singhi & Co. are proposed for appointment for a term of five consecutive years from the conclusion of the 104th AGM until the conclusion of the 109th AGM, and cost audit remuneration is ratified annually by members.
- Transition all manufacturing units towards achieving Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) status, as part of a structured water-risk evaluation with a dedicated governance mechanism to monitor water performance regularly
- Eliminated dependence on coal by utilising jute process waste (jute caddies) as a renewable biomass fuel, materially reducing greenhouse gas emissions and local air pollutants while addressing long-standing waste-disposal challenges — a circular-economy substitution that reduces exposure to fuel price volatility
- Treated effluent is being utilised for combustion purposes in boilers, reducing freshwater dependency and contributing to circular water usage within operations
- Gradual integration of renewable energy sources such as rooftop solar, alongside energy efficiency initiatives through process optimisation and modernisation of machinery
- Optimise water usage, promote conservation practices and enhance rainwater harvesting systems
- Installation and effective maintenance of air pollution control devices for boilers and processing units, with regular monitoring of stack and ambient air emissions and periodic reporting and internal audits to ensure compliance
- Adoption of cleaner fuels and preventive equipment maintenance to minimise fugitive emissions
- Periodic climate and energy risk assessments to enhance operational resilience
- Biodiversity protection measures through plantation drives around operational sites
- BRSR reported on a standalone basis with limited assurance obtained from TUV SUD
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Gloster's standalone manufacturing base at Bauria, Howrah, West Bengal comprises four integrated business units spread over more than 175 acres, supported by a workforce of more than 4,500 persons, and is capable of producing around 60,000 metric tonnes of jute textiles and products annually. The principal recent expansion has been through wholly owned subsidiary Gloster Nuvo Limited (GNL), incorporated on 27th January 2020 for manufacturing jute and allied products: GNL implemented its phase I project with a total capital investment of more than Rs. 270 crores to manufacture 92 MT of jute and allied products per day, procuring modern imported machineries for value-added products; commercial production commenced on 30th March 2024 and GNL is presently producing around 104 MT of jute and allied products including fine yarns per day. GNL has since also started a retail business manufacturing lifestyle products, shopping bags, upholstery and home furnishing products under the name "Unit - Globag". Looking forward, the Board approved on 31st December 2025 a collaboration with Gujarat State Co-operative Marketing Federation (GUJCOMASOL) to form a joint venture SPV named "GUJCO Gloster Limited" for manufacturing and supplying jute gunny bags — promoting sustainability, rural employment and eco-friendly packaging — with Gloster holding 49% and GUJCOMASOL 51%; the SPV is in the process of being incorporated. In parallel, the Board approved on 12th November 2025 a modified Scheme of amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiaries Gloster Lifestyle Limited and Gloster Specialities Limited into Gloster Limited, subject to necessary approvals. There were no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the financial year end and the date of the report, and no change in the nature of business during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Raw jute price was significantly higher in the current financial year versus 2024-25; the estimate for the upcoming crop is encouraging as area under cultivation has increased and weather has been favourable, and the price of raw jute in the ensuing season shall correct significantly
- Carry-over crop in the ensuing season is virtually nil
- Demand from Government is expected to be very strong
- With prices correcting, the Company hopes to win back some of the export markets lost to Bangladesh
- Demand for industrial products like Hessian & Sacking and promotional jute goods like lifestyle products and other made-ups has grown over the years and is expected to see further growth
- Rising concerns for reducing carbon footprints opens doors for greater use of biodegradable and sustainable products made from natural fibres
- Export demand has been reviving lately
- Compulsory packing norms under JPMA stand at 100% of food grains and 20% of sugar production, with the notification valid up to 30th June 2026
- Retail business is expected to play a pivotal role in driving value-added growth, increasing brand visibility and positioning jute as a preferred sustainable lifestyle material
